{{nihongo|'''Haritsuna Shrine'''|針綱神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Inuyama, Aichi|ar|إنوياما (آيتشي)|azb|اینویاما، آیچی|ce|Инуяма|ceb|Inuyama-shi|ckb|ئینویاما، ئایچی|cs|Inujama|de|Inuyama|el|Ινουγιάμα (Άιτσι)|es|Inuyama (Aichi)|eu|Inuyama (Aichi)|fa|اینویاما، آیچی|fi|Inuyama|fr|Inuyama|gl|Inuyama|hy|Ինույամա|id|Inuyama, Aichi|it|Inuyama|ja|犬山市|kk|Инуяма|ko|이누야마시|mdf|Инуяма|mg|Inuyama|mzn|اینویاما، آیچی|nl|Inuyama|pl|Inuyama|pnb|انویامہ|pt|Inuyama|ro|Inuyama|ru|Инуяма|simple|Inuyama, Aichi|sv|Inuyama|tg|Инуяма|th|อินูยามะ|tl|Inuyama, Aichi|tr|Inuyama|tt|Инуяма|uk|Інуяма|ur|انویاما، ایچی|vi|Inuyama, Aichi|war|Inuyama, Aichi|zh|犬山市|zh_classical|犬山市|zh_min_nan|Inuyama-chhī|zh_yue|犬山|qid=Q503411}}, {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}. It is identified with "Haritsuna Shrine" in Niwa District, Owari Province, listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. {{nihongo|'''Haritsuna Shrine'''|針綱神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

It is said to grant blessings for safe childbirth and conception. This tradition comes from {{ill|1537|Q6461|qid=Q6461}} ({{ill|Tenbun|ckb|تێنبون|fa|تنبون|fi|Tenbun-kausi|fr|Ère Tenbun|it|Tenbun|ja|天文 (元号)|ko|덴분|pt|Tenbun|ru|Тэмбун|simple|Tenbun|sr|Тенбун|sv|Tenbun|tr|Tenbun|zh|天文 (日本)|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 6), when {{ill|Oda Nobuyasu|Q11608286|qid=Q11608286}} dedicated a pair of guardian dogs carved by his own hand to pray for safe childbirth. Since then, praying on the Day of the Dog has been considered auspicious.

Like {{ill|三光稲荷神社|Q11354440|qid=Q11354440}}, it stands near the southern entrance route up to {{ill|Inuyama Castle|Q1155484|qid=Q1155484}}. The {{ill|Inuyama Festival|Q11571216|qid=Q11571216}} is this shrine's festival.

== History ==
Until the Edo period it was called '''Hakusan-sha''' and was the guardian shrine of Inuyama Castle. Its foundation date is unknown. Its original site was near the castle keep, but in {{ill|1537|Q6461|qid=Q6461}} ({{ill|Tenbun|ckb|تێنبون|fa|تنبون|fi|Tenbun-kausi|fr|Ère Tenbun|it|Tenbun|ja|天文 (元号)|ko|덴분|pt|Tenbun|ru|Тэмбун|simple|Tenbun|sr|Тенбун|sv|Tenbun|tr|Tenbun|zh|天文 (日本)|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 6) it was moved by {{ill|Oda Nobuyasu|Q11608286|qid=Q11608286}} to Hakusan-daira (the hill where {{ill|Narita-san Temple|Q11495646|qid=Q11495646}} now stands). In {{ill|1606|Q6747|qid=Q6747}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 11), castle lord {{ill|Ogasawara Yoshitsugu|Q10860025|qid=Q10860025}} moved it to Naguri-machi in the castle town. In {{ill|1635|Q6879|qid=Q6879}} ({{ill|Kan'ei|Q1192913|qid=Q1192913}} 12), parade floats/processions from Shimohonmachi and Uoyamachi were presented for the shrine festival. In {{ill|1641|Q6907|qid=Q6907}} (Kanei 18), Shimohonmachi changed its horse tower to a wheeled float and dedicated mechanical dolls; this became the prototype of the Inuyama Festival. In {{ill|1649|Q6945|qid=Q6945}} ({{ill|Keian|fa|کی‌آن|fr|Ère Keian|ja|慶安|ko|게이안|ru|Кэйан|simple|Keian|sr|Кеиан|sv|Keian|th|เคอัง|tr|Keian|zh|慶安 (日本)|qid=Q1146135}} 2), castle lord {{ill|Naruse Masatora|Q11495574|qid=Q11495574}} encouraged wheeled floats and processions, making the festival even more active.

In the mid-Edo period, scholars including {{ill|Amano Sadakage|Q6535030|qid=Q6535030}} advanced the theory that this shrine corresponds to Niwa District's "Haritsuna Shrine" in the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho,'' and this became the prevailing view. Based on this, in {{ill|1775|Q7700|qid=Q7700}} (An'ei 4) it was renamed "Hakusan Haritsuna Daimyojin," and officially came to be called Haritsuna Shrine. However, this identification has dissenting views: {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}} argued that the original Haritsuna Shrine was Ueno-mura Tenjin (present {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tateno Shrine}}). ''Tokusen Shinmeicho'' does not mention a specific identification. In the Meiji period it became a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}; in {{ill|1876|Q7766|qid=Q7766}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 8) it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. In {{ill|1882|Q7812|qid=Q7812}} (Meiji 15) it was moved to the current site and became a prefectural shrine.

== Transportation ==
*15-minute walk from {{ill|Inuyama Station|Q6059394|qid=Q6059394}} on the {{ill|Meitetsu Inuyama Line|Q6810411|qid=Q6810411}}
*10-minute walk from {{ill|Inuyama-Yūen Station|Q6059388|qid=Q6059388}} on the Meitetsu Inuyama Line
*Get off at "Inuyama Castle" stop on the {{ill|Kakamigahara City Fureai Bus|Q11412316|qid=Q11412316}} holiday circular route (runs weekends/holidays)

== Other ==
{{commons category|Haritsuna-jinja}}
*The guardian dogs carved by Oda Nobuyasu for safe-childbirth prayer are also said to have been modeled after {{ill|Oda Hirochika|Q11608371|qid=Q11608371}}. Oda Hirochika built {{ill|Kinoshita Castle|Q11517925|qid=Q11517925}} in Inuyama in {{ill|1469|Q6566|qid=Q6566}} ({{ill|Bunmei|Q1193544|qid=Q1193544|lt=Bunmei}} 1), and also built a fort near present Inuyama Castle, forming the prototype of Inuyama Castle.
